outcome: A spell cast for its overload cost has every "target" replaced with "each", so it affects all matching objects on resolution instead of one target.
An overloaded spell requires no targets and affects objects that could not have been chosen as legal targets, such as hexproof creatures.
The overload text change turns the spell's single-target effect into an all-objects effect.
note: Text-changing effect is not captured; its result is visible in the resolution events.
